notes.calculate: Standard calculator tool: no state is read or written. Restricted the character set (digits, + - * /, parentheses, dot, space) before evaluating, and rounded the numeric result to 2 decimals returned as a string.
notes.cancel_pending_order: Assumed refunds are recorded as new 'refund' rows in payment_transactions mirroring the original 'payment' rows; if no payment transaction exists, the order's payment_method_id and the sum of order_items prices are used. Authentication and ownership checks come from the policy.
notes.exchange_delivered_order_items: Gift card balance is validated but not deducted (charge happens at exchange completion, matching the original retail domain behaviour). No payment_transactions row is created since the exchange is only requested. Authentication is only enforced as an ownership mismatch check when the session already records an authenticated user.
notes.find_user_id_by_name_zip: Name matching is case-insensitive; zip is compared exactly. Returns the user id string, matching the original retail tool behaviour.
notes.find_user_id_by_email: Matching is case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace. Returns the user_id string (as in the standard retail tool) rather than a dict.
notes.get_order_details: Read-only lookup; no authentication check is enforced inside the tool since the session gate is an agent-level policy and no auth precondition is stated in the tool description. Missing orders raise ValueError via _find.
notes.get_product_details: Read-only lookup; raises ValueError via _find when the product id does not exist. Variants are keyed by item_id (tau-bench retail format). No authentication check enforced here since the tool only exposes generic catalog data, not user-specific information.
notes.get_item_details: Read-only lookup; raises ValueError via _find when the item id does not exist. Included the product name from the products collection for context since items only carry a product_id.
notes.get_user_details: Read-only lookup; raises ValueError via _find when the user id does not exist. Session authentication is not re-checked here since authentication is performed by the find_user_* tools. Gift cards report balance; other methods report brand/last_four.
notes.list_all_product_types: Returns a name -> product_id dict (matching the tau-bench retail convention); duplicate product names would collapse, which is acceptable since names are unique among the 50 product types.
notes.modify_pending_order_address: Assumed authentication must be checked via session and that the order must belong to the authenticated user. Returns the updated order (with its order_items) as a dict.
notes.modify_pending_order_items: Assumed session authentication is required and the order must belong to the authenticated user. Since orders have no 'payment_history' collection, the price-difference charge/refund is recorded in payment_transactions and orders.payment_method_id is set to the provided method. Order status set to 'pending (items modified)' with items_modified=True to block further modification.
notes.modify_pending_order_payment: Assumed the order total equals net (payments minus refunds) of existing payment_transactions, falling back to the sum of order_items prices. Transaction ids are generated as 'txn_%07d'. Also enforced session authentication and that the order belongs to the authenticated user.
notes.modify_user_address: Assumed the policy's authentication requirement is a precondition: the session must be authenticated and the authenticated user id must match user_id. Returns the updated user profile dict.
notes.return_delivered_order_items: Schema has no dedicated 'return_payment_method_id' field, so the refund destination is stored in orders.exchange_payment_method_id (closest existing field). Duplicate item ids are matched against distinct order_item rows. Gift-card refunds are not credited immediately here since no transaction/balance update field is specified for returns.
notes.transfer_to_human_agents: Assumed no authentication precondition for transfers (a user who cannot be authenticated may still need a human). Assumed a repeat transfer in the same session is an error, and that a non-empty summary is required.
